newsitem.title: USA: McDonald's June same-store sales off - analysts.
newsitem.headline: McDonald's June same-store sales off - analysts.

text.p: McDonald's Corp, which a month ago canceled most of its nationwide Campaign 55 price promotion, saw a decline in June same-store sales of up to eight percent, analysts said.
This follows a drop in same-store sales in May of an estimated five percent.
"Unquestionably it (was) a down month," Natwest Securities analyst Damon Brundage said. "(June same-store sales were) down eight percent or a touch more for the month."
McDonald's declined to comment on its June sales.
For the first 21 days in June, McDonald's same-store sales were down an estimated 7.5 percent, analysts said.
Morgan Stanley analyst Howard Penney said he estimated June same-store sales -- measuring results from units open at least a year -- were down about five to seven percent.

The calendar also played a role in the estimated drop in McDonald's June same store sales. June 1996 included five full weekends of Friday through Sunday, while June 1997 had only four full weekends and a Sunday.
McDonald's outlets typically reap half their weekly sales between Friday and Sunday, analysts said.

Also impacting sales for the month was McDonald's decision in early June to cancel its Campaign 55 price promotion for lunch and dinner. Under that campaign, McDonald's offered hamburgers for $0.55 when consumers also bought beverages and french fries.

That cancellation left McDonald's without a product-based national promotion. Its ongoing marketing promotion is tied in with the new "Hercules" animated movie under a long-term alliance with Walt Disney Co.
McDonald's, meanwhile, has a variety of regional promotions aimed at boosting sales, including specially priced Big Mac hamburgers and double- and triple-cheesburgers, franchisee sources said.

For example, McDonald's is testing the "Quarterpounder Big and Tasty," a quarterpound hamburger with tomato, in Los Angeles and a "few restaurants" in the Sacramento area, according to spokeswoman Anna Rozenich.
"There are no plans to do more than a limited market testing at this time," she added.
